items.iast:
maharṣīṇāṁ bhṛgur ahaṁ
girām asmy ekam akṣaram
yajñānāṁ japa-yajño 'smi
sthāvarāṇāṁ himālayaḥ
items.translation:
Of the great sages I am Bhṛgu; of vibrations I am the transcendental
oṁ. Of sacrifices I am the chanting of the holy names [japa-yajña],
and of immovable things I am the Himalayas.
items.chanting_connection:
Krishna Himself names japa as the sacrifice He IS. Each bead is not
a personal exercise — it is Krishna performing yajña through your
tongue. Sit with that before the first round.
items.source: Bhagavad-gītā As It Is 10.25, Prabhupada's purport

items.iast:
nāma cintāmaṇiḥ kṛṣṇaś
caitanya-rasa-vigrahaḥ
pūrṇaḥ śuddho nitya-mukto
'bhinnatvān nāma-nāminoḥ
items.translation:
The holy name of Krishna is a transcendentally blissful bestower
of all spiritual benediction, for it is Krishna Himself, the
reservoir of all pleasure. Krishna's name is complete, pure, and
eternally liberated, because the name and the named are non-different.
items.mood_brought: faith in the Name's identity with Krishna
items.chanting_connection:
Chant with the understanding that the syllables you utter ARE
Krishna Himself. There is no gap between Name and Named — the
meeting has already happened. Speak with attention; He listens.
items.source: Caitanya Caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 17.133, citing Padma Purāṇa

items.iast:
harer nāma harer nāma
harer nāmaiva kevalam
kalau nāsty eva nāsty eva
nāsty eva gatir anyathā
items.translation:
In this age of quarrel and hypocrisy the only means of deliverance
is chanting the holy name of the Lord. There is no other way.
There is no other way. There is no other way.
items.mood_brought: settled clarity — there is nothing else to do
items.chanting_connection:
Stop searching for an alternative process, an upgrade, a parallel
path. The threefold repetition seals the search. Begin japa as if
this single instruction is the whole of dharma — because in this
age it is.
items.source: Caitanya Caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā 17.21, citing Bṛhan-nāradīya Purāṇa

items.iast:
ceto-darpaṇa-mārjanaṁ bhava-mahā-dāvāgni-nirvāpaṇaṁ
śreyaḥ-kairava-candrikā-vitaraṇaṁ vidyā-vadhū-jīvanam
ānandāmbudhi-vardhanaṁ prati-padaṁ pūrṇāmṛtāsvādanaṁ
sarvātma-snapanaṁ paraṁ vijayate śrī-kṛṣṇa-saṅkīrtanam
items.translation:
Let there be all victory for the chanting of the holy name of
Lord Kṛṣṇa, which can cleanse the mirror of the heart and stop
the miseries of the blazing fire of material existence. That
chanting is the waxing moon that spreads the white lotus of good
fortune, the life and soul of all transcendental knowledge, the
ever-expanding ocean of bliss, full nectar at every step, and a
bath for the soul.
items.chanting_connection:
Eight effects in one verse: mirror cleaned, forest fire extinguished,
moon rises, knowledge revealed, ocean expanded, nectar tasted at
every step, bath in nectar. Begin japa as if these effects are
already happening — they are.

items.iast:
tṛṇād api sunīcena
taror api sahiṣṇunā
amāninā mānadena
kīrtanīyaḥ sadā hariḥ
items.translation:
One should chant the holy name of the Lord in a humble state of
mind, thinking oneself lower than the straw in the street; one
should be more tolerant than a tree, devoid of all sense of false
prestige, and ready to offer all respect to others. In such a state
of mind one can chant the holy name of the Lord constantly.
items.chanting_connection:
This is not a goal AFTER chanting — it is the precondition.
Take 30 seconds to actually feel: lower than straw, more tolerant
than a tree, expecting no honor, offering all honor. Then begin.

items.iast:
na dhanaṁ na janaṁ na sundarīṁ
kavitāṁ vā jagad-īśa kāmaye
mama janmani janmanīśvare
bhavatād bhaktir ahaitukī tvayi
items.translation:
O almighty Lord, I have no desire to accumulate wealth, nor do I
desire beautiful women, nor do I want any number of followers. I
only want Your causeless devotional service, birth after birth.
items.chanting_connection:
The four objects renounced (wealth, women/followers, fame as a
poet) are the four poles around which the conditioned mind moves
even during japa. Let go of them once, before japa, and the rounds
move freely.

items.iast:
jīvera 'svarūpa' haya — kṛṣṇera 'nitya-dāsa'
kṛṣṇera 'taṭasthā-śakti' 'bhedābheda-prakāśa'
items.translation:
It is the living entity's constitutional position to be an
eternal servant of Krishna because he is the marginal energy of
Krishna and a manifestation simultaneously one with and different
from the Lord.
items.chanting_connection:
Before chanting, recover the relation: not seeker, not student,
not aspirant — eternal servant. The hand picks up the beads from
THAT identity, not from any other.

items.iast:
kṛṣṇa-mantra haite habe saṁsāra-mocana
kṛṣṇa-nāma haite pābe kṛṣṇera caraṇa
items.translation:
Simply by chanting the holy name of Krishna one can obtain freedom
from material existence. Indeed, simply by chanting the Hare
Krishna mantra one will be able to see the lotus feet of the Lord.
items.chanting_connection:
Caitanya Mahāprabhu states the outcome in two lines: freedom
from saṁsāra, and the lotus feet of Krishna. Begin japa with the
destination in view, not with anxiety about whether you'll arrive.

items.iast:
ataeva śrī-kṛṣṇa-nāma nā āise tāra mukhe
sphure nā kabhu bhakti-yoga-rasera mukhe
items.translation:
Therefore the holy name of Krishna does not appear in the mouth
of one who is averse to devotional service, nor does the taste of
the mellow of bhakti-yoga ever manifest for such a person.
items.chanting_connection:
The Name does not enter every mouth equally — it requires sukṛti.
Approach japa not as something you do TO the Name, but as
something the Name allows you to do. Petition first; then chant.
items.source: Caitanya Caritāmṛta, Ādi-līlā (cf. 1.96 — Prabhupada's purport thread)

items.iast:
'sādhu-saṅga', 'sādhu-saṅga' — sarva-śāstre kaya
lava-mātra sādhu-saṅge sarva-siddhi haya
items.translation:
The verdict of all revealed scriptures is that by even a moment's
association with a pure devotee, one can attain all success.
items.chanting_connection:
Whatever chanting capacity you have today, came from devotee
association — gurus, books, kīrtana. Remember a single devotee
before japa. Their mood will support yours.

items.iast:
kṛṣṇa-varṇaṁ tviṣākṛṣṇaṁ
sāṅgopāṅgāstra-pārṣadam
yajñaiḥ saṅkīrtana-prāyair
yajanti hi su-medhasaḥ
items.translation:
In the age of Kali, intelligent persons perform congregational
chanting to worship the incarnation of Godhead who constantly
sings the names of Kṛṣṇa. Although His complexion is not blackish,
He is Kṛṣṇa Himself. He is accompanied by His associates, servants,
weapons, and confidential companions.
items.chanting_connection:
The chanting you do now is what intelligent souls of this age have
ALWAYS done. You are part of a stream that includes Caitanya
Mahāprabhu, the Six Goswāmīs, your own guru-paramparā. Step in.

items.iast:
śṛṇvatāṁ sva-kathāḥ kṛṣṇaḥ
puṇya-śravaṇa-kīrtanaḥ
hṛdy antaḥ-stho hy abhadrāṇi
vidhunoti suhṛt-satām
items.translation:
Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Personality of Godhead, who is the Paramātmā in
everyone's heart and the benefactor of the truthful devotee,
cleanses the desire for material enjoyment from the heart of the
devotee who has developed the urge to hear His messages, which
are in themselves virtuous when properly heard and chanted.
items.chanting_connection:
You are not the one cleaning the heart — Krishna inside the heart
is. Your job is to provide the input: the hearing, the chanting.
He does the rest. Begin japa as a contribution, not a battle.

items.iast:
naṣṭa-prāyeṣv abhadreṣu
nityaṁ bhāgavata-sevayā
bhagavaty uttama-śloke
bhaktir bhavati naiṣṭhikī
items.translation:
By regular attendance in classes on the Bhāgavatam and by
rendering of service to the pure devotee, all that is troublesome
to the heart is almost completely destroyed, and loving service
unto the Personality of Godhead, who is praised with
transcendental songs, is established as an irrevocable fact.
items.chanting_connection:
Each day's japa is one deposit. The cumulative effect is what
establishes naiṣṭhika-bhakti. Don't expect today's rounds to do
what only a year of days can do. Just deposit today's.

items.iast:
tad-vāg-visargo janatāgha-viplavo
yasmin prati-ślokam abaddhavaty api
nāmāny anantasya yaśo-'ṅkitāni yat
śṛṇvanti gāyanti gṛṇanti sādhavaḥ
items.translation:
On the other hand, that literature which is full of descriptions
of the transcendental glories of the name, fame, forms, pastimes,
etc., of the unlimited Supreme Lord is a different creation,
full of transcendental words directed toward bringing about a
revolution in the impious lives of this world's misdirected
civilization. Such transcendental literatures, even though
imperfectly composed, are heard, sung, and accepted by purified
men who are thoroughly honest.
items.chanting_connection:
Even imperfect chanting, if it bears the Name, revolutionises the
sinful condition. Don't wait for perfection to begin. Begin
imperfectly; the Name does the revolution.

items.iast:
tyaktvā sva-dharmaṁ caraṇāmbujaṁ harer
bhajann apakvo 'tha patet tato yadi
yatra kva vābhadram abhūd amuṣya kiṁ
ko vārtha āpto 'bhajatāṁ sva-dharmataḥ
items.translation:
One who has forsaken his material occupations to engage in the
devotional service of the Lord may sometimes fall down while in
an immature stage, yet there is no danger of his being unsuccessful.
On the other hand, a non-devotee, though fully engaged in
occupational duties, does not gain anything.
items.chanting_connection:
If you chant inattentively today and fall short of your standard
tomorrow, the deposit is not lost. The deposit IS the practice.
Begin without hedging against failure.

items.iast:
etāvān eva loke 'smin
puṁsāṁ dharmaḥ paraḥ smṛtaḥ
bhakti-yogo bhagavati
tan-nāma-grahaṇādibhiḥ
items.translation:
Devotional service, beginning with the chanting of the holy name
of the Lord, is the ultimate religious principle for the living
entity in human society.
items.chanting_connection:
All other dharmas are decorations on this central act. Yamarāja
himself instructs his servants on this point. Beginning your
rounds, you are doing the central thing — not a side practice.

items.iast:
śravaṇaṁ kīrtanaṁ viṣṇoḥ
smaraṇaṁ pāda-sevanam
arcanaṁ vandanaṁ dāsyaṁ
sakhyam ātma-nivedanam
iti puṁsārpitā viṣṇau
bhaktiś cen nava-lakṣaṇā
items.translation:
Prahlāda Mahārāja said: Hearing and chanting about the
transcendental holy name, form, qualities, paraphernalia and
pastimes of Lord Viṣṇu, remembering them, serving the lotus feet
of the Lord, offering the Lord respectful worship with sixteen
types of paraphernalia, offering prayers to the Lord, becoming
His servant, considering the Lord one's best friend, and
surrendering everything unto Him — these nine processes are
accepted as pure devotional service.
items.chanting_connection:
Prahlāda lists hearing and chanting FIRST — before remembrance,
service, prayer. You are now doing the foundational two. Everything
else builds from these two. Begin with that hierarchy clear.

items.iast:
jñāne prayāsam udapāsya namanta eva
jīvanti san-mukharitāṁ bhavadīya-vārtām
sthāne sthitāḥ śruti-gatāṁ tanu-vāṅ-manobhir
ye prāyaśo 'jita jito 'py asi tais tri-lokyām
items.translation:
My dear Lord, those devotees who have completely given up
attempts to mentally speculate about You and instead simply hear
about You from the lips of pure devotees, and who pass their
lives engaged in dedicating their body, mind and words in Your
service while remaining in their own occupational positions —
such persons certainly conquer You, although You are otherwise
unconquerable.
items.chanting_connection:
Stop thinking ABOUT chanting and just hear the chanting. The
sastras' verdict is that those who hear from devotees with
body-mind-words conquer the unconquerable. Hearing is the
single key.

items.iast:
evaṁ-vrataḥ sva-priya-nāma-kīrtyā
jātānurāgo druta-citta uccaiḥ
hasaty atho roditi rauti gāyaty
unmāda-van nṛtyati loka-bāhyaḥ
items.translation:
By chanting the holy name of the Supreme Lord, one comes to the
stage of love of God. Then the devotee is fixed in his vow as an
eternal servant of the Lord, and he gradually becomes attached to
a particular name and form of the Lord. As his heart melts in
ecstatic love, he laughs very loudly or cries or shouts. Sometimes
he sings and dances like a madman, indifferent to society.
items.chanting_connection:
This is what the Name eventually does — not in one round, but as
a trajectory. You are not chanting for nothing. There is a final
condition the rounds are walking toward. Walk one step today.

items.iast:
kaler doṣa-nidhe rājann
asti hy eko mahān guṇaḥ
kīrtanād eva kṛṣṇasya
mukta-saṅgaḥ paraṁ vrajet
items.translation:
My dear King, although Kali-yuga is an ocean of faults, there is
still one good quality about this age: simply by chanting the
Hare Krishna mahā-mantra, one can become free from material
bondage and be promoted to the transcendental kingdom.
items.chanting_connection:
This age makes most practices impossibly hard. But ONE practice
is made easier than ever before. You are sitting at the exact
junction where the loophole is widest. Take it.

items.iast:
anta-kāle ca mām eva
smaran muktvā kalevaram
yaḥ prayāti sa mad-bhāvaṁ
yāti nāsty atra saṁśayaḥ
items.translation:
And whoever, at the time of death, quits his body, remembering
Me alone, at once attains My nature. Of this there is no doubt.
items.chanting_connection:
Every round of japa is a rehearsal for the last moment. What
you train the mind to fall into now is what it will fall into
then. Today's rounds shape the final moment.

items.iast:
tasmāt sarveṣu kāleṣu
mām anusmara yudhya ca
mayy arpita-mano-buddhir
mām evaiṣyasy asaṁśayam
items.translation:
Therefore, Arjuna, you should always think of Me in the form of
Krishna and at the same time carry out your prescribed duty of
fighting. With your activities dedicated to Me and your mind and
intelligence fixed on Me, you will attain Me without doubt.
items.chanting_connection:
Krishna's instruction is not "stop fighting and only think of Me."
It is BOTH — duty AND remembrance. Japa is the practice of doing
both. Today's rounds are training for today's actions.

items.iast:
satataṁ kīrtayanto māṁ
yatantaś ca dṛḍha-vratāḥ
namasyantaś ca māṁ bhaktyā
nitya-yuktā upāsate
items.translation:
Always chanting My glories, endeavoring with great determination,
bowing down before Me, these great souls perpetually worship Me
with devotion.
items.chanting_connection:
Three activities of mahātmās: constant chanting, determined
endeavor, devoted obeisance. You are about to do the first.
Recognize: you are in the company of mahātmās the moment you
pick up the beads.

items.iast:
patraṁ puṣpaṁ phalaṁ toyaṁ
yo me bhaktyā prayacchati
tad ahaṁ bhakty-upahṛtam
aśnāmi prayatātmanaḥ
items.translation:
If one offers Me with love and devotion a leaf, a flower, fruit,
or water, I will accept it.
items.chanting_connection:
Krishna accepts a leaf with love. He accepts your imperfect
chanting with love too. Don't postpone the offering until it is
grand. Offer today's rounds, however they sound.

items.iast:
api cet su-durācāro
bhajate mām ananya-bhāk
sādhur eva sa mantavyaḥ
samyag vyavasito hi saḥ
items.translation:
Even if one commits the most abominable action, if he is engaged
in devotional service he is to be considered saintly because he
is properly situated in his determination.
items.chanting_connection:
Krishna does not assess your worthiness by your worst action.
He assesses by your direction. Today's chanting is the direction.
Begin without rehearsing your faults.

items.iast:
mac-cittā mad-gata-prāṇā
bodhayantaḥ parasparam
kathayantaś ca māṁ nityam
tuṣyanti ca ramanti ca
items.translation:
The thoughts of My pure devotees dwell in Me, their lives are
surrendered to Me, and they derive great satisfaction and bliss
from enlightening one another and conversing about Me.
items.chanting_connection:
The condition you aspire to is the condition Krishna describes
here: mind in Him, life surrendered to Him, conversation about
Him. Today's japa is one act in service of this condition.

items.iast:
sarva-dharmān parityajya
mām ekaṁ śaraṇaṁ vraja
ahaṁ tvāṁ sarva-pāpebhyo
mokṣayiṣyāmi mā śucaḥ
items.translation:
Abandon all varieties of religion and just surrender unto Me. I
shall deliver you from all sinful reactions. Do not fear.
items.chanting_connection:
The cap of the Gītā: surrender, and don't fear. Sit before japa
and let this verse work. The fear of doing it wrong, the fear of
not measuring up — Krishna directly addresses these. Mā śucaḥ.

items.iast:
ātmārāmāś ca munayo
nirgranthā apy urukrame
kurvanty ahaitukīṁ bhaktim
ity ambhūta-guṇo hariḥ
items.translation:
Those who are self-satisfied and free from all material desires
are nevertheless attracted to the loving service of Śrī Kṛṣṇa,
whose qualities are transcendental and whose activities are
wonderful. Hari, the Personality of Godhead, possesses such
qualities that He attracts even the liberated souls.
items.chanting_connection:
Even the ātmārāmas — those who have completed self-realization —
continue to chant. Chanting is not a means you discard upon
arrival. It IS the arrival. Begin with that long view.

items.iast:
jihvā na vakti bhagavad-guṇa-nāmadheyaṁ
cetaś ca na smarati tac-caraṇāravindam
kṛṣṇāya no namati yac-chira ekadāpi
tān ānayadhvam asato 'kṛta-viṣṇu-kṛtyān
items.translation:
My dear servants, please bring to me only those sinful persons
who do not use their tongues to chant the holy name and qualities
of Kṛṣṇa, whose hearts do not remember the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa
even once, and whose heads do not bow down even once before Lord
Kṛṣṇa.
items.mood_brought: what counts and what does not
items.chanting_connection:
Yamarāja's criterion is the simplest possible: did the tongue
chant, did the heart remember, did the head bow — even once?
Today's rounds satisfy all three. You step out of his jurisdiction.

items.iast:
yugāyitaṁ nimeṣeṇa
cakṣuṣā prāvṛṣāyitam
śūnyāyitaṁ jagat sarvaṁ
govinda-viraheṇa me
items.translation:
O Govinda! Feeling Your separation, I am considering a moment to
be like twelve years or more. Tears are flowing from my eyes like
torrents of rain, and I am feeling all vacant in the world in
Your absence.
items.chanting_connection:
The most advanced devotional emotion is not satisfaction but
separation-longing. Don't seek a placid japa. If a single
sincere call of "Govinda" leaves an ache, that ache is the
progress.

items.iast:
āśliṣya vā pāda-ratāṁ pinaṣṭu mām
adarśanān marma-hatāṁ karotu vā
yathā tathā vā vidadhātu lampaṭo
mām eva nāthas tu sa eva nāparaḥ
items.translation:
I know no one but Krishna as my Lord, and He shall remain so even
if He handles me roughly by His embrace or makes me brokenhearted
by not being present before me. He is completely free to do
anything and everything, for He is always my worshipful Lord,
unconditionally.
items.chanting_connection:
The pinnacle of the Śikṣāṣṭakam: He may embrace, He may break
the heart by absence, He may do anything — He is still the Lord.
Begin japa with this unconditional disposition, asking nothing.
